headline: High prompt-injection and data-leakage risk: Devin’s autonomous cloud workspace can feed Semantic Kernel plugins/MCP with untrusted content and shared state.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin can use MCP, browsers, shell, and shared integrations, so its outputs may contain raw external content. Semantic Kernel consumes plugin/function outputs via MCP/OpenAPI and shared memory-store patterns, creating a plausible instruction-hijack path. The pair’s documented surfaces make this interaction credible even without a specific bridge implementation.
conditions: IF Devin forwards web or repo content into Semantic Kernel prompts or plugins without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF Semantic Kernel treats plugin output as instructions rather than data, attacker-controlled text can steer actions.
mitigations: Add a strict content-to-instruction separator in the handoff prompt.
Strip markdown/code fences and executable directives before passing text.
Require explicit allowlists for MCP/plugin calls.
Insert a human review step for any externally sourced content.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to every cross-agent message.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, docs, and secrets; Semantic Kernel can send context to Azure OpenAI/OpenAI/Hugging Face and plugin credentials. If they share a workspace or memory store, sensitive material can flow from Devin into B’s model/provider calls. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF both agents access the same repo, chat thread, or memory store, leakage risk increases.
IF Semantic Kernel forwards Devin-originated context to a third-party model provider, sensitive data may leave the workspace.
mitigations: Remove secrets from shared context before handoff.
Use separate workspaces or namespaces for each agent.
Disable provider calls for sensitive tasks.
Review logs for cross-agent payloads.
requires-engineering: enforce redaction at the integration boundary.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin has unrestricted cloud-workspace shell, filesystem write, and git modification; Semantic Kernel also has filesystem write and broad API/MCP access. If both operate on the same mutable repo or shared resource, concurrent writes and state drift are likely. The profiles show overlapping write surfaces but no locking, so the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository branch or workspace directory, conflicts can occur.
IF either agent mutates shared plugin state without locks, last-writer-wins corruption is possible.
mitigations: Assign separate branches or directories.
Serialize writes with a lock file or queue.
Use read-only mode for one agent during edits.
Run a diff check before merge.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control to shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin is an autonomous planner-executor, while Semantic Kernel is a function-calling orchestration layer that can act on plugin outputs. If Devin’s generated facts or code suggestions are consumed by B without verification, errors can cascade into downstream tool calls. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Semantic Kernel uses Devin’s output as authoritative input to plugins or OpenAPI tools, errors can propagate.
IF Devin produces hallucinated facts that B converts into actions, downstream mistakes can multiply.
mitigations: Require a validation step before any tool call.
Cross-check Devin outputs against source files or APIs.
Limit B to read-only summarization for untrusted inputs.
Log provenance for each claim used in actions.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for all handoffs.

E_compliance.rationale: Devin touches team chat, issue trackers, docs, and secrets; Semantic Kernel can route context to external model providers and plugin credentials. That creates a plausible retention/residency mismatch if the same data class is forwarded from A to B. The profiles do not specify HIPAA/GDPR boundaries, so medium is the prudent level.
conditions: IF EU personal data or regulated content is passed from Devin into a non-approved model provider, compliance risk arises.
IF logs or provider retention differ between the two agents, subject-rights handling may diverge.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared prompts.
Disable external provider calls for sensitive workflows.
Review retention settings for both agents.
Document data-flow boundaries.
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing by data class.
